title: a conditional capability argument naming two classes pins neither, so the layer is opaque — including when the two arms are structurally identical and the checker type reduces to one
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Satisfaction': 'When the compiler knows the complete closure, an unsatisfied capability MUST be a compile error.' — and its contrapositive, which is what `SMITHERS2104` is for: when the compiler does NOT know the closure it must say so rather than assume one. A conditional whose two arms name two different classes pins no single nominal context key, so the layer's provided set is unknown at compile time. WHY THERE ARE TWO PROVIDES AND WHY THE SECOND CARRIES THE MECHANISM: `Directory` and `Clock` are differently shaped, so `typeof Directory | typeof Clock` survives in the checker's type as a real union and a TYPE-directed resolver refuses the first provide too. `Journal` is declared STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL to `Directory` and is a different nominal key, so `typeof Directory | typeof Journal` subtype-reduces to `typeof Directory` and nothing in the type remembers that there was ever a second arm. A type-directed resolver therefore refuses the first and silently ACCEPTS the second, picking a key by coincidence — which is exactly what the Go fork did before 2026-08-27: one diagnostic here, not two. Both provides are needed. The second alone would not show that the first still refuses; the first alone is satisfied by a resolver that reads types, which is the resolver this case exists to reject. WHAT THIS CASE PINS: two `SMITHERS2104`, one at each `Layer.succeed`. Because the judge compares the declared set exactly, it also pins that neither provide draws a SECOND diagnostic beside its refusal — in particular not `SMITHERS2101`, which would be the claim that the closure IS known and was found short. `directory as never` is in both service arguments on purpose: it makes the capability argument the only expression in each call that could be the thing refused, so a diagnostic at column 3 cannot be about the service. NO `messageContains` IS DECLARED: `SMITHERS2104` carries no payload the specification promises, the code and the authored position are the whole contract, and conformance/README.md reserves the field for rules whose payload IS the promise. Its siblings at the LAYER position — `opaque-layer-is-rejected` and `a-mutable-layer-binding-is-opaque` — declare none either; this is the same answer one argument in. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CONTAIN: a REASSIGNED binding. `let C = Directory; C = Twin; Layer.succeed(C, directory)` is accepted and panics at run time on BOTH backends today. That is not a hole this rule left — it is `SMITHERS2106`'s own pre-existing residual, and the identical shape at the `X.context()` receiver behaves the same way, untouched; closing it needs a new rule that has to move both walks together, and `const`-ness alone would over-refuse aliases that run. It is pinned as an explicit known-residual UNIT test (`poc/src/language/layer-capability-argument.test.ts`) and deliberately kept out of the corpus, because a corpus case over that shape could only encode today's acceptance as the contract — which is the opposite of what a case is for. `06-layers/a-mutable-layer-binding-is-opaque` is the reassigned binding at the LAYER position, where the answer IS settled and IS refusal; the capability argument does not have that answer yet. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the SECOND diagnostic's column from 3 to 17 — attributing the refusal to the conditional expression rather than to the `Layer.succeed` call, a plausible attribution rather than a nonsense one — turns the case red on BOTH backends with `[SMITHERS2104@31:3, SMITHERS2104@36:3] != [SMITHERS2104@31:3, SMITHERS2104@36:17]` printed on each. The SECOND row is mutated deliberately: it is the subtype-reduced twin arm the fork accepted before this revision, so a mutation on the first row alone would have been satisfied by the pre-fix behaviour and would have proved nothing about the half that was broken. The expectation was restored byte-identically (sha256 8f5fc8086596d0944019f4e98aa7a79856dff9745d2012e10e5d680abac78c1e before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — this sentence is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently). The mutator refuses to run at all unless the case is green on BOTH backends first AND its search string occurs exactly once in the file; both refusals were exercised against this case rather than assumed, because a search string that matches nothing mutates nothing and comes back green.
